AngleUnits.description: The data units of an angle.

oneOf.description: 360 to a turn; tick labels carry a degree sign.
2π to a turn; tick labels are written as multiples of π.

The given number to a turn, which is finite and positive: for example the number of
categories of a radar chart, 24 hours or 12 months.

Artist.description:
A drawable node of an axes.

Every artist has a node identifier, an optional label drawn beside it in a legend,
and a visibility flag. An artist refers to its data by the node identifiers of data
arrays of the figure. Future plot types are added as new variants, each with a line in
the declaration of the kinds of node, which generates the methods of `Artist`.

oneOf.description:
Data points drawn as a line, as markers or as both, optionally sized and coloured
by data (plot, plot3, loglog, semilogx, semilogy, scatter, scatter3).
Isolines or filled isobands of a gridded field (contour, contourf, contour3).
Arrows at data points (quiver, quiver3).

A gridded surface of faces (surf, mesh, and surface, which in 2D axes is a
pseudocolour plot).
A raster of true-colour pixels (image with a true-colour array).

A raster of numbers, each mapped to a colour through a colour scale (image with
an indexed array, imagesc).

Rectangles that rise from a base to each value, one per position along a category
axis (bar, barh).
A stepped outline through values held between edges or at samples (stairs, step).

A grid of rectangular cells between edges, each coloured by its value through a
colour scale (heatmap, pcolormesh on a rectilinear grid, histogram2).

Aspect.description:
The ratios of the drawn length of one data unit of y, and of z, to that of one data unit
of x, as MATLAB's `daspect` gives them.

On a logarithmic axis the data unit is one decade, so `Equal` on log–log axes draws a
decade of x and a decade of y at the same length. A 2D axes uses the ratio of y alone.

oneOf.description:
The plot area, or the box of a 3D axes, keeps its own shape and the limits are those
of the data, whatever the ratio of their lengths.

One data unit is drawn at the same length along every axis, which is
`Ratio { y: 1.0, z: 1.0 }`.

One data unit of y is drawn `y` times as long as one data unit of x, and one data
unit of z `z` times as long. Both are finite and positive; `z` is ignored by a 2D
axes but validated all the same.

y.description: How many times as long a unit of y is drawn as a unit of x.

z.description: How many times as long a unit of z is drawn as a unit of x, in a 3D axes.

AspectAdjust.description: How an axes keeps a fixed [`Aspect`].

oneOf.description:
The limits are kept as they are, manual or automatic. A 2D axes shrinks its plot area
along one dimension, centred in the space the layout gives it; a 3D axes gives the
sides of its box the lengths of the scaled ranges of its axes.

The plot area of a 2D axes, and the cube of a 3D axes, keep their shape, and the
limits of the axes that are too short for it are widened symmetrically about their
centres. Manual limits are the least range shown.

Axes.description: A plotting region placed in one or more cells of the figure's tile layout.

artists.description: The artists drawn in this axes, in drawing order.

aspect.description:
The ratios of the length of one data unit of y, and of z, to the length of one data
unit of x.

aspect_adjust.description:
How a fixed aspect is kept: by shaping the plot area or the box, or by widening
limits. Ignored when the aspect is `Auto`.

box.description:
Whether the full outline of the plot box is drawn, rather than only the
edges that carry tick labels: all twelve edges of a three-dimensional box,
rather than the three that carry its ticks, and the top and wall of a
cylindrical axes, rather than only its floor.

cell.description: The cells of the figure's tile layout that the axes occupies.

colorbar.description:
The colourbar drawn inside the plot area along one of its edges, or `null` when the
axes shows none.

id.description: The node identifier of the axes, unique within the figure.

legend.description: The legend, or `null` when no legend is shown.

projection.description: Whether the axes is two- or three-dimensional, with its 3D view.

title.description: The title drawn above the axes.

title_align.description:
How the title is aligned with the plot area: centred over it, or with its left or
right edge on the left or right edge of the plot area.

x.description: The horizontal axis in 2D, or the first horizontal axis in 3D.

y.description: The vertical axis in 2D, or the second horizontal axis in 3D.

z.description: The vertical axis in 3D; ignored by 2D axes.

Axis.description: One coordinate axis of an axes.

grid.description: Whether grid lines are drawn at the major ticks of this axis.

limits.description: The range of data values shown along the axis.

reverse.description:
Whether the axis runs from its upper limit to its lower limit: from left to
right for a horizontal axis, and from bottom to top for a vertical axis. The
limits themselves keep `min < max`; only the direction in which they are drawn
changes.

scale.description: The mapping from data values to positions along the axis.

side.description:
The side of the plot on which the axis draws its line, tick marks, tick labels and
label. Two-dimensional and three-dimensional Cartesian axes honour it on every
axis, and cylindrical axes on z; polar axes, spherical axes and the angle and
radius of cylindrical axes ignore it.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is [`AxisSide::Low`], and is Low when
JSON omits it.

tick_label_angle.description:
The angle of every tick label of the axis, in degrees anticlockwise from
horizontal, about the end of the label nearest its tick; any finite number. A
three-dimensional axes ignores it.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 0, and is 0 when JSON omits it.

tick_labels.description: What is written at the major ticks of the axis.

ticks.description: Where the major ticks of the axis are placed.

visible.description:
Whether the axis is drawn. A hidden axis draws no spine (the edges of the plot box
along it), ticks, tick labels or label, and no space is reserved for them; its grid
lines still follow [`grid`](Axis::grid), and its limits, scale and ticks still
place the data. In a three-dimensional axes the edges of the box are drawn
whatever the visibility.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is true, and is true when JSON omits it.

AxisLink.description:
A group of axes whose limits along one dimension are kept equal.

For each dimension, the groups of a figure are disjoint: an axes belongs to at
most one group per dimension.

axes.description: The identifiers of the linked axes.

dimension.description: The dimension whose limits are linked.

AxisSide.description:
The side of the plot on which an axis draws its line, tick marks, tick labels and label,
across the direction in which the axis runs on the page.

The side is a side of the page, not an end of the data range: reversing an axis does not
move the axes drawn along it. Tick labels and the axis label lie on the outside of the
line, away from the plot; through the middle they lie on the low side of the line.

oneOf.description:
The left of the plot for an axis that runs up the page, and the bottom for one that
runs across it: the lowest box edge on the page for the x and y axes of a
three-dimensional axes, the leftmost vertical edge for its z axis, and the left wall
of a cylinder for the z axis of cylindrical axes.

Through the middle of the plot: through the centre of the floor of a
three-dimensional axes, and up the axis of the cylinder of cylindrical axes.

The right of the plot for an axis that runs up the page, and the top for one that
runs across it: the highest box edge on the page for the x and y axes of a
three-dimensional axes, the rightmost vertical edge for its z axis, and the right
wall of a cylinder for the z axis of cylindrical axes.

Bar.description:
A series of bars: one rectangle for each position along the category axis, which
runs along the value axis from a base for the length of its value (bar, barh).

The positions, the values and any base or widths given as data hold one entry per bar
and must have the same number of elements. Each bar is centred along the category axis
at its position plus the offset of the series, and is as wide as its width. It runs
from its base to its base plus its value, so that a value is a length, as in Matplotlib
and Plotly, and a negative value extends the other way. A bar whose position or value
is not finite is not drawn, and a non-finite position takes no part in the pitch. Bars
colour individual bars as a series colours individual markers: with colour data of one
value per bar, mapped through a colour scale of any kind, a colormapped face or edge
takes the colour of each bar's value.

A bar series draws exactly the bars it describes and lays out nothing itself: grouped
and stacked bars are ordinary series whose widths, offsets and bases place them side by
side or on one another, as the facade's `bars` helper writes them (ADR 0026).

base.description: Where each bar starts along the value axis.

binning.description:
How the histogram that the bars draw was binned from its samples, or `None` for bars
that were not made from samples (ADR 0029). The record is descriptive: it is read
by datatips to report the count and density of each bin and is never edited.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

color_data.description:
The values that colour the bars through their colour scale, one per bar, or `None`
for bars of fixed colours.

color_scale.description:
The colour scale through which the colour data is mapped. Bars with colour data
must name one; bars without colour data map nothing.

edge.description:
The style of the outline of every bar. Its colour is none for no outline, a fixed
colour, automatic for the colour of the series (as an automatic marker edge is), or
colormapped, which gives the outline of each bar the colour of its bar's value
through the colour scale.

edge_opacity.description:
The opacity of the outlines, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies
the alpha of their colours.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

face.description:
The colour of the bars: automatic for the next colour of the colour order, which
is the colour of the series, a fixed colour, none, or colormapped, which gives each
bar the colour of its value of the colour data through the colour scale. Without
colour data a colormapped face has no value to map and is drawn as an automatic one.

face_opacity.description:
The opacity of the faces, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies the
alpha of their colours.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

margin.description:
The fraction of the span of the series along the value axis, from the lowest to the
highest of its bases and ends, that the automatic limits of the value axis add
beyond the ends of the bars, on each side where an end lies away from its base, so
that the longest bar does not touch the box while bars rising from 0 keep 0 at the
edge of the axis; a finite number from 0. Manual limits ignore it.

offset.description: How far the centre of each bar lies from its position along the category axis.

orientation.description: Whether the bars stand upright or lie flat.

positions.description:
The position of each bar along the category axis, one value per bar: the category
or value to which the bar belongs, before the offset is applied.

values.description:
The length of each bar from its base along the value axis, one value per bar; a
negative length extends the other way, and a value that is not finite draws no bar.

width.description: How wide each bar is along the category axis.

BarOffset.description:
How far the centre of each bar of a series lies from its position along the category
axis.

oneOf.description:
A multiple of the width of each bar, which keeps the columns of a grouped chart side
by side whatever their width: a finite number, negative to the low side.
A distance in data units, the same for every bar: a finite number.

BarWidth.description: How wide each bar of a series is along the category axis.

oneOf.description:
A fraction of the pitch: the smallest distance between neighbouring distinct finite
positions of the series, or 1 when there is a single distinct position. The
fraction is a finite positive number; 1 draws bars that touch.
The same width for every bar, in data units: a finite positive number.

One width for each bar, in data units, each a finite positive number; this is how a
histogram of unequal bins is drawn.

BinRule.description: A named rule that chooses the number of bins of a histogram from its samples.

oneOf.description: The rule that the binning library chooses by default.
Sturges' rule: `⌈log₂ n⌉ + 1` bins.
Scott's rule, from the standard deviation of the samples.
The Freedman–Diaconis rule, from the interquartile range of the samples.
The square root of the number of samples.
One bin for each whole number in the range.

Binning.description:
How the bins of a histogram of one dimension were made from its samples (ADR 0029).

The record is descriptive: the binned values are stored on the bars or stairs that
draw them, and nothing is computed from the record except the count and density of a
bin that a datatip reports, from the width of the bin between its resolved edges.

edges.description:
The data array of the edges that the specification resolved to: one more than the
bins, finite and strictly increasing. Stairs refer to the array of their own edges.

excluded_non_finite.description: The number of samples left out because they were not finite.

excluded_out_of_range.description: The number of samples left out because they lay outside the range.

normalization.description: How the counts of the bins were normalised into the values drawn.

range.description:
The range of sample values that was binned, as `[low, high]`, or `None` when the
range of the samples was used.

total.description:
The total the values were normalised by, finite and not negative: the number of
samples counted into the bins, or, for one of several histograms normalised
together, as the members of a stack are, the number counted into the bins of all
of them.

Binning2d.description: How the bins of a histogram of two dimensions were made from its samples (ADR 0029).

excluded_non_finite.description: The number of samples left out because they were not finite.

excluded_out_of_range.description: The number of samples left out because they lay outside the ranges.

min_count.description:
The count below which a bin was left empty, or `None` when every bin was drawn: a
number of samples, finite and not negative.

normalization.description: How the counts of the bins were normalised into the values drawn.

total.description: The number of samples counted into the bins: finite and not negative.

x_bins.description: How the bins along x were specified.

x_edges.description:
The data array of the edges along x that the specification resolved to: one more
than the columns, finite and strictly increasing. Cells on explicit column edges
refer to the array of those edges.

x_range.description:
The range of sample values along x that was binned, or `None` for the range of the
samples.

y_bins.description: How the bins along y were specified.

y_edges.description:
The data array of the edges along y that the specification resolved to: one more
than the rows, finite and strictly increasing. Cells on explicit row edges refer to
the array of those edges.

y_range.description:
The range of sample values along y that was binned, or `None` for the range of the
samples.

Bins.description: How the bins of a histogram were specified.

oneOf.description: A number of bins of equal width across the range: at least 1.
Bins of the given width across the range: a finite positive number.
The edges of the bins: at least two, finite and strictly increasing.
A number of bins of equal width chosen by a named rule.

CategoricalColorScale.description:
A categorical colour scale: labelled categories of which a whole number `i` from 0 to
the number of categories less one takes category `i`, drawn as separate outlined
squares, each with its label.

Any other finite value, a fractional one included, lies outside the categories and
follows `outside`.

outside.description:
What is drawn for a value that names no category; strict by default, so that such
a value is a validation error.

Cell.description:
A rectangular block of cells in the figure's tile layout.

Rows and columns are numbered from zero, starting at the top-left cell.

col.description: The zero-based index of the leftmost column occupied.

col_span.description: The number of columns occupied; at least one.

row.description: The zero-based index of the top row occupied.

row_span.description: The number of rows occupied; at least one.

CellEdges.description: The edges of the columns or rows of cells.

oneOf.description:
Cell `k` spans `k − 0.5` to `k + 0.5`, so the centres lie at 0, 1, 2 and so on, as
the pixels of an image without a range do.

The edges given as data: one more than the cells, finite and strictly monotonic,
increasing or decreasing.

CellGap.description:
The fractions of the extent of each cell left empty along x and along y, measured on
the page and shared equally by the two sides of the cell; each is a finite number from
0 up to, but not including, 1.

x.description: The fraction of the width of each cell left empty.

y.description: The fraction of the height of each cell left empty.

Cells.description:
A grid of rectangular cells, each coloured by its value through a colour scale
(heatmap, histogram2, pcolormesh on a rectilinear grid).

Cell `(j, i)` holds the value in row `j` and column `i` of `values` and spans the
column edges `i` and `i + 1` along x and the row edges `j` and `j + 1` along y, so that
row 0 lies between the first two row edges. The fraction `gap` of each cell's extent is
left empty, measured on the page so that cells on a logarithmic axis remain
symmetric. Cells are valid only in a two-dimensional axes.

alpha.description:
The alpha of every cell, a two-dimensional array with the same shape as `values`,
or `None` for cells that are uniformly opaque before
[`face_opacity`](Cells::face_opacity) applies. The array may hold floating-point values from
0 to 1 or 8-bit values from 0 to 255, as the alpha of a scalar image may.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

binning.description:
How the two-dimensional histogram that the cells draw was binned from its samples,
or `None` for cells that were not made from samples (ADR 0029). The record is
descriptive: it is read by datatips to report the count and density of each cell and
is never edited.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

color_scale.description:
The colour scale through which the values are mapped. Cells always map their
values, so a figure in which they name no scale is invalid.

columns.description: The edges of the columns along x.

edge.description:
The style of the outline of every cell; a colour of none draws no outline, and an
automatic or colormapped colour gives each outline the colour of its cell.

edge_opacity.description:
The opacity of the outlines of the cells, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which
multiplies the alpha of their colour.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

face_opacity.description:
The opacity of the cells, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies the
alpha of every cell: the alpha of its colour and, when present, its
[`alpha`](Cells::alpha).

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

gap.description: The fraction of each cell's extent left empty, along x and along y.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

rows.description: The edges of the rows along y.

values.description:
The values, a two-dimensional array of shape `[ny, nx]` with one value per cell.
The array may hold floating-point values or 8-bit values; an 8-bit value is mapped
as the whole number it denotes.

Color.description: An sRGB colour with straight alpha, written as #rrggbb when opaque or #rrggbbaa otherwise.

ColorCategory.description:
One category of a categorical colour scale: its colour and its label, which every key
that shows the scale draws beside the colour.

label.description:
The label drawn beside the colour; required, so that every category can be told
apart in a key.

ColorScale.description:
A colour scale: a node of the figure that turns numbers into colours, which
colour-mapped artists name by its identifier.

In JSON the kind is an object whose `type` names the kind and whose `value` holds it,
such as `{"type": "continuous", "value": {"colormap": ..., "limits": ...}}`.

id.description: The node identifier of the scale, unique within the figure.

kind.description: How values become colours and how the scale is drawn.

non_finite.description:
What is drawn for a value that is NaN or infinite, on every kind of scale. The
policy is transparent by default, because a non-finite value is the author's way
of saying that nothing is drawn there.

title.description:
The title drawn with the scale: above a colourbar that shows it, and as the label
of a bar item that shows it in a legend.

ColorScaleKind.description: How a colour scale turns values into colours, which also fixes how it is drawn.

oneOf.description: A colormap interpolated between limits, drawn as a smooth bar.
Bands between edges, each in one colour of a colormap, drawn as a bar of bands.

A palette of which a whole number `i` takes entry `i`, drawn as a bar of adjoining
blocks.

Labelled categories of which a whole number `i` takes category `i`, drawn as
separate outlined squares.

ColorScaleLevels.description: The edges of the bands of a discrete colour scale.

oneOf.description:
Edges at nice values from the lower limit to the upper limit, which are the first
and last edges.

count.description: The approximate number of bands; at least one.

limits.description:
The range that the edges span. Automatic limits are the range of the values
mapped through the scale, as for a continuous scale.

oneOf.description: Edges given explicitly.

values.description:
The edges: at least two, finite, strictly increasing, and positive under a
logarithmic norm.

ColorScaleNorm.description:
The space in which a continuous or discrete colour scale places values between its
limits.

oneOf.description: Positions are proportional to values.

Positions are proportional to the base-10 logarithm of values; a value that is
not positive lies below the range.

ColorScaleOutOfRange.description:
One category of values that a colour scale cannot place within its range: the values
below or above the range of a continuous or discrete scale, the values outside the
entries of an indexed or categorical scale, or the values that are not finite.

The type has no single default, because the default policy differs by category:
clamping below and above, strict outside the entries, and transparent for non-finite
values. [`ColorScaleOutOfRange::new`] builds a category of a given policy.

label.description:
The label of the key square, or `None` for the default label: `> upper` above
the range, `< lower` below it, `NaN / Inf` for non-finite values and
`Out of range` outside the entries, with the limits formatted as the ticks are.

policy.description: What is drawn for a value of the category.

show_key.description:
Whether a colourbar that shows the scale draws a key square for the category,
separate from the bar. Keys are off by default.

ColorSpec.description: How a colour is chosen for a stroke, fill or marker.

oneOf.description:
The renderer chooses the colour: for series this is the next colour of the
axes colour order (Okabe–Ito), inside a marker of a series it is the colour of
the series' line, and on the isolines of a contour, the faces and edges of a surface
and the outlines of cells, which have no colour of their own, it is the colour mapped
through the artist's colour scale, as for `colormapped`.
A fixed colour.
Nothing is drawn.

The colour is mapped from the data value through the colour scale that the
artist names.

ColorbarOrientation.description: The direction in which a panel colourbar runs.

oneOf.description:
The bar stands upright, with low values at the bottom and its tick labels on the
right.
The bar lies flat, with low values at the left and its tick labels below.

ColorbarTitlePlacement.description:
Where the title of a colour scale is drawn beside a colourbar of the scale.

The field that holds it is named `title_placement`, not `title`, because a title is
drawn text and this is where the scale's title is drawn.

oneOf.description:
Beyond the tick labels, on their side of the bar, centred on its length. Along a
standing bar the title is rotated a quarter turn counter-clockwise, so that it reads
from bottom to top, as the label of a y axis does.

As an upright heading beside the bar: above a standing bar (above a standing panel
bar, in the margin above the first row the panel spans) and above a lying panel bar.
On a lying bar inside an axes, whose tick labels face the interior of the plot area,
the heading lies on the side of the bar away from them: below a bar along the south
edge and above a bar along the north edge.

Colormap.description: The palette that a continuous or discrete colour scale interpolates.

oneOf.description: A bundled colormap.

reverse.description: Whether the colormap runs from its last colour to its first.

oneOf.description:
A list of colours, interpolated linearly in sRGB from the first, at the start of
the scale, to the last, at its end.

ColormapName.description: The name of a bundled colormap, which a [`Colormap`](crate::Colormap) names.

oneOf.description: The perceptually uniform blue–green–yellow colormap.

The perceptually uniform blue–yellow colormap designed for colour-vision
deficiency.
The perceptually uniform black–purple–cream colormap.
The perceptually uniform black–red–yellow colormap.
The perceptually uniform blue–purple–yellow colormap.
The diverging blue–white–red colormap.
The linear black–white colormap.

ContinuousColorScale.description:
A continuous colour scale: a colormap interpolated between two limits, in linear or
logarithmic space.

A value exactly at a limit lies inside the range.

above.description: What is drawn for a value above the upper limit; clamped by default.

below.description:
What is drawn for a value below the lower limit; clamped by default. Under a
logarithmic norm a value that is not positive lies below the range.

colormap.description: The palette that the scale interpolates.

limits.description:
The values mapped to the first and last colours of the colormap. Automatic limits
are the exact range of the finite values (the positive finite values under a
logarithmic norm) of every artist that maps values through the scale, in every
axes, hidden artists included. Manual limits must be finite and strictly
increasing, and positive under a logarithmic norm.

norm.description: Whether values are interpolated in linear or logarithmic space.

tick_labels.description: What is written at the ticks of a colourbar that shows the scale.

ticks.description: Where the ticks of a colourbar that shows the scale are placed.

Contour.description: Isolines or filled isobands of a scalar field sampled on a grid.

color_scale.description:
The colour scale through which levels and bands are coloured. A contour whose
bands are filled, or whose isolines are colormapped or automatic, must name one.

fill.description:
Whether the bands between levels are filled (contourf) rather than only the
isolines drawn (contour).

fill_opacity.description:
The opacity of the filled bands, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which
multiplies the alpha of their colour.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

grid.description: The grid on which the field is sampled.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

levels.description:
The field values at which isolines are drawn or between which bands are filled, or
`None` for the levels of the colour scale: the band edges of a discrete scale, and
ten automatic levels otherwise, so that a contour and the bar of its discrete scale
cannot disagree.

line.description:
The style of the isolines; a colormapped colour takes the colour of each
isoline's level through the colour scale.

line_opacity.description:
The opacity of the isolines, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies
the alpha of their colour.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

placement.description: Where the contours are placed in 3D axes.

z.description: The field values, a two-dimensional array of shape `[ny, nx]`.

ContourPlacement.description: Where contours are placed in 3D axes.

oneOf.description: All contours lie in one horizontal plane (contour, contourf).

z.description:
The height of the plane in 3D axes, or `null` for the bottom of the z
axis; ignored by 2D axes.

oneOf.description:
Each isoline is drawn at the height of its level (contour3); valid only in
3D axes.

Coords.description:
How the values of one dimension of a series are placed in a 2D axes.

A series places each dimension independently, so that a dimension in data
coordinates and one in axes-fraction coordinates make a blended placement, as
Matplotlib's blended transforms do: a reference line spanning the axes at a data
value, or markers along an edge of the axes at data positions.

oneOf.description:
The values are data, placed through the limits and scale of the axis, and take
part in its automatic limits.

The values are fractions of the plot area along the dimension: 0 is its left or
bottom edge and 1 its right or top edge, whatever the limits, scale or direction
of the axis. They take no part in the automatic limits of the axis, and values
outside `[0, 1]` lie beyond the plot area.

DashStyle.description: The dash pattern of a stroked line.

oneOf.description: A continuous line.
A line of dashes.
A line of dots.
A line of alternating dashes and dots.
A line of dashes, each followed by two dots.
A line of long dashes.
No line is drawn.

DataArray.description:
A numeric array of the figure, which artists refer to by its node identifier.

A data array is a node of the figure, beside its axes and panels, in the identifier
space that every node shares. Artists refer to their data by identifier rather than
containing it, so that artists of any axes share one array and the array is stored
once. The values of an array change only through the data edits
([`Edit::ReplaceData`](crate::Edit::ReplaceData) and
[`Edit::AppendData`](crate::Edit::AppendData)), and its name is its only settable
property.

id.description: The node identifier of the array, unique within the figure.

name.description:
The name that identifies the array to tools such as the inspector, or `None` when
it has none. The name is never drawn and constrains nothing: two arrays may share
a name, and a name may be empty.

Dimension.description: A coordinate dimension of an axes.

oneOf.description: The x axis.
The y axis.
The z axis.

DiscreteColorScale.description:
A discrete colour scale: bands between edges, each drawn in one colour of a colormap.

With k bands, band i takes the colour of the colormap at i / (k − 1), so both ends of
the colormap are used; a single band takes the colour at the start. A value exactly on
an edge between two bands belongs to the upper band, and a value exactly at the first
or last edge lies inside the range. Every artist that names the scale is banded, a
smooth surface included, so that the bar that shows the scale is truthful.

above.description: What is drawn for a value above the last edge; clamped by default.

below.description: What is drawn for a value below the first edge; clamped by default.

colormap.description: The palette from which the bands take their colours.

norm.description:
Whether band edges are chosen, and the colormap sampled, in linear or logarithmic
space.

tick_labels.description: What is written at the ticks of a colourbar that shows the scale.

ticks.description:
Where the ticks of a colourbar that shows the scale are placed; automatic ticks
are one per band edge.

Edit.description:
A change to a figure.

In JSON an edit is an object whose `type` names the kind of edit in `snake_case`,
alongside the fields of that kind, such as
`{"type": "set", "node": 3, "path": "x.limits", "value": {"type": "limits", ...}}`.

oneOf.description: Replaces the value of a property of a node.

node.description: The node whose property is set.

path.description: The path of the property within the node.

value.description:
The new value, whose type must be that of the property, or
[`Value::Unset`] to clear an optional property.

oneOf.description:
Inserts a node with its subtree: a data array, an axes or a panel into the figure,
or an artist into an axes.

index.description:
The position in the parent's list of the node's kind at which the node is
inserted, from zero to the length of the list, or `None` to append it.

node.description:
The node, whose identifier and whose descendants' identifiers must not be in
use in the figure.

parent.description:
The parent: the figure for a data array, an axes or a panel, or an axes for an
artist.

oneOf.description: Removes a node and its subtree.

node.description: The data array, axes, artist or panel to remove.

oneOf.description:
Moves a data array, an axes or a panel within the figure's list of its kind, or an
artist within its axes or to another axes.

index.description:
The position in the new parent's list after the node has been removed from
its old position, from zero to the length of that list, or `None` to append.

node.description: The data array, axes, artist or panel to move.

parent.description:
The new parent: the figure for a data array, an axes or a panel, or an axes for
an artist.

oneOf.description:
Replaces the values of an existing data array, which keeps its identifier and its
name, so that every artist that refers to it draws the new values.
Appends entries to an existing data array along its first dimension.

array.description:
The entries to append, whose shape after the first dimension and whose
element type must equal those of the existing array.

retain.description:
When set, only the last `retain` entries along the first dimension are kept
after appending, which gives a rolling window for streamed data.

Embolden.description:
How much heavier than designed a figure is drawn.

Emboldening changes how the figure is rendered, not what it says: text written in the
regular weight stays regular and bold text stays bold relative to it, while every
step draws text heavier and multiplies the thickness of every line and edge. Marker
sizes, tick lengths and spacing are unchanged, because a marker's size can represent
data. Heavier steps suit projection; the default suits print.

oneOf.description: Drawn as designed.

Text drawn as heavy as STIX Two Text Medium, and lines and edges thickened in
proportion.

Text drawn as heavy as STIX Two Text SemiBold, and lines and edges thickened in
proportion.

FigureSize.description: The physical size of a figure.

FontSetId.description: The identifier of a bundled font set.

oneOf.description: STIX Two Text for text and STIX Two Math for mathematics.

Grid.description: The grid on which a field of shape `[ny, nx]` is sampled.

oneOf.description: An axis-aligned grid defined by one coordinate vector per axis.

x.description: The x coordinates of the columns, an array of `nx` values.

y.description: The y coordinates of the rows, an array of `ny` values.

oneOf.description: A structured grid whose every node has its own coordinates.

x.description: The x coordinate of every node, an array of shape `[ny, nx]`.

y.description: The y coordinate of every node, an array of shape `[ny, nx]`.

HistNorm.description: How the counts of the bins of a histogram are normalised into the values drawn.

oneOf.description: The number of samples in each bin.
The fraction of the samples in each bin, so that the values sum to 1.
The percentage of the samples in each bin, so that the values sum to 100.
The number of samples in each bin divided by its width (or area).

The probability density of each bin: its count divided by the total and by its
width (or area), so that the areas sum to 1.
The number of samples in each bin and every bin before it.

The fraction of the samples in each bin and every bin before it: the empirical
cumulative distribution function.

Image.description:
A true-colour image: a raster of pixels, each with its own colour (image with a
true-colour array).

An image is drawn as flat, uninterpolated pixels rather than as a mesh, so it is
planar: it lies in one of the coordinate planes of its axes, where its
[`placement`](Image::placement) puts it.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

opacity.description:
The opacity of the image, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies
the alpha of every pixel: its alpha component in a four-channel array, and 1 in
a three-channel array. A true-colour image has no separate alpha array, because
a four-channel array already gives every pixel its own alpha.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

pixels.description:
The pixels, a three-dimensional array of shape `[ny, nx, 3]` (the red, green and
blue components of every pixel) or `[ny, nx, 4]` (with an alpha component), so
that the components of the pixel in row `j` and column `i` start at index
`(j * nx + i) * channels`. The array may hold floating-point components from 0
to 1 or 8-bit components from 0 to 255. A pixel with a non-finite component is
transparent.

placement.description: Where the pixels lie in the axes.

ImagePlacement.description:
Where the pixels of an image lie in its axes: the plane of the image, and the
coordinates of its pixel centres along the two axes of that plane.

Along each axis of the plane the pixels are placed by the centres of the first and
last pixels, from which the pitch between centres follows, and the image covers half
a pitch beyond each centre. An absent range places the centres at 0, 1, …, n − 1, so
an image of `nx` columns covers −0.5 to nx − 0.5 along the first axis of its plane.
Row 0 of the array lies at the centre of the first row and column 0 at the centre of
the first column, whichever way the ranges run.

columns.description:
The centres of the first and last columns along the first axis of the plane, or
`None` for centres at 0 to nx − 1.

plane.description: The plane in which the image lies, with its offset along the third axis.

rows.description:
The centres of the first and last rows along the second axis of the plane, or
`None` for centres at 0 to ny − 1.

ImagePlane.description:
The plane of an axes in which an image lies, with the offset of the plane along the
third axis.

The columns of the image run along the first axis of the plane and its rows along
the second. The offset is the coordinate of the plane along the third axis, or
`None` for the low end of that axis. A two-dimensional axes shows only the xy plane
and ignores its offset; the xz and yz planes are the walls of a three-dimensional
axes and are valid only there.

oneOf.description: The plane of the x and y axes: the floor of a three-dimensional axes.

z.description:
The height of the plane, or `None` for the bottom of the z axis; ignored by
two-dimensional axes.

oneOf.description: The plane of the x and z axes: a wall of a three-dimensional axes.

y.description: The y coordinate of the plane, or `None` for the low end of the y axis.

oneOf.description: The plane of the y and z axes: the other wall of a three-dimensional axes.

x.description: The x coordinate of the plane, or `None` for the low end of the x axis.

IndexedColorScale.description:
An indexed colour scale: a palette of which a whole number `i` from 0 to the number of
entries less one takes entry `i`, such as the 256-entry palette of an indexed image.

Any other finite value, a fractional one included, lies outside the entries and
follows `outside`. An array of 8-bit values holds whole numbers only.

colors.description: The entries of the palette; at least one.

outside.description:
What is drawn for a value that names no entry; strict by default, so that such a
value is a validation error.

tick_labels.description: What is written at the ticks of a colourbar that shows the scale.

ticks.description:
Where the ticks of a colourbar that shows the scale are placed, at the centres of
the entries; automatic ticks fall on whole numbers only.

InsideColorbar.description:
A colourbar drawn inside the plot area of an axes, along one of its edges, over the
artists. It takes no margin: the plot area keeps its size whether or not the bar is shown.

length.description:
The length of the bar, together with any keys it shows, as a fraction of the edge it
lies along, centred on it: a finite number greater than 0 and at most 1.

scale.description: The colour scale that the bar shows.

side.description:
The edge of the plot area along which the bar lies, which also sets its orientation:
horizontal along the south and north edges, vertical along the east and west edges.

title_placement.description: Where the title of the scale is drawn beside the bar, within the box behind it.

InsideColorbarSide.description:
The edge of the plot area along which an inside colourbar lies. Its tick labels face the
interior of the plot area.

oneOf.description: Along the bottom edge, horizontal.
Along the top edge, horizontal.
Along the right edge, vertical.
Along the left edge, vertical.

InsideLegend.description: A legend drawn inside the plot area of its axes.

boxed.description: Whether the legend is drawn with a background and outline.

entries.description:
Which entries the legend lists, and in what order: the labelled artists of its axes
in artist order, or an explicit list of items. An item that names an artist must
name an artist of the same axes.

The property is omitted from JSON when the entries are automatic.

layout.description: How the entries are arranged in columns.

location.description: Where the legend is placed inside the plot area.

Interpreter.description: How the source of a [`Text`] is interpreted.

oneOf.description: Mixed plain text and `$…$` LaTeX mathematics.
Plain text, rendered literally, including any dollar signs.

Legend.description:
The legend of an axes, which lists the artists of the axes that have a label.

The entries of an axes are shown either in a legend drawn inside its own plot area or
in a panel of the figure that holds a legend, never in both. In JSON a legend is an object whose
`type` names the variant and whose `value` holds its content, such as
`{"type": "inside", "value": {"location": "north_east", ...}}` or
`{"type": "panel", "value": 7}`.

oneOf.description: The entries are listed in a legend drawn inside the plot area of the axes.

The entries are listed in the panel of the figure with this node identifier, which
must hold a legend, together with the entries of every other axes that names the
same panel.

LegendEntries.description:
Which entries a legend lists, and in what order.

In JSON the entries are an object whose `type` names the variant, such as
`{"type": "auto"}` or `{"type": "explicit", "value": [...]}`.

oneOf.description:
Every artist with a label, in the order of the legend: for a legend inside a plot
area, the artists of its axes in artist order; for the legend of a panel, the
artists of every axes that names the panel, in the reading order of the layout,
with the entries of the same label and look merged into one.

Exactly these items, in this order. The order of the items is independent of the
order in which the artists are drawn, so a series drawn last, on top of the
others, can be listed first.

LegendEntryColumns.description:
The number of columns in which the entries of a legend are arranged.

In JSON the number is an object whose `type` names the variant, such as
`{"type": "auto"}` or `{"type": "count", "value": 3}`.

oneOf.description: The fewest columns in which the entries fit the height available to the legend.
A fixed number of columns, which must be at least one.

LegendEntryLayout.description: How the entries of a legend are arranged in columns.

order.description: The order in which the entries fill the columns.

LegendEntryOrder.description: The order in which the entries of a legend fill its columns.

oneOf.description: Each column is filled from top to bottom before the next column is started.
Each row is filled from left to right before the next row is started.

LegendItem.description: One item of an explicit list of legend entries.

content.description:
What the item lists: an artist, a label and sample that stand for no artist, or a
colour scale.

full_row.description:
Whether the item spans every column of the legend, on a row of its own at its
position in the list. The label of such an item does not set the width of any
column.

LegendItemContent.description:
What an item of an explicit list of legend entries lists.

In JSON the content is an object whose `type` names the variant, such as
`{"type": "artist", "value": 12}`,
`{"type": "custom", "value": {"label": {...}, "sample": {...}}}` or
`{"type": "color_scale", "value": {"scale": 4, "rows": 5}}`.

oneOf.description:
The artist with this node identifier, labelled by its label beside the sample
drawn for it. Clicking the item in the viewer hides or shows the artist.

A label beside a sample, standing for no artist, such as the meaning of a marker
shape that many artists share. Clicking the item does nothing.

label.description: The label shown beside the sample.

sample.description: The sample drawn beside the label.

oneOf.description:
The colour scale with this node identifier, which may be any scale of the figure.
A categorical scale is listed as one entry per category, labelled with the label
of the category beside a swatch of its colour, followed by an entry for each of
its out-of-range keys that is shown; these are ordinary entries, which a legend
panel merges with any other entry of the same label and look, and a legend inside
a plot area merges with nothing. A continuous, discrete or indexed scale
is drawn as a vertical bar `rows` entry rows long in one column, ticked on the side
of the labels and titled along the bar beyond its tick labels, as a colourbar of the
scale is drawn; each of its out-of-range keys that is shown is an entry row of its
own, a swatch beside a label, directly above the bar (the above key) or below it
(the below or outside key, then the non-finite key). On a row of its own, the bar is
horizontal, spans the width of the legend and is titled below its tick labels.
Clicking the item does nothing, because a scale is not an artist.

rows.description:
The number of entry rows along which a standing bar runs: at least 1. It is
ignored by a categorical scale, which lists one entry per category, and by an
item on a row of its own, whose bar lies across the legend; it is validated
whatever the kind of the scale or the row of the item.

scale.description: The node identifier of the colour scale.

LegendLocation.description: The placement of a legend inside the plot area of its axes.

oneOf.description: The top-right corner.
The top-left corner.
The bottom-right corner.
The bottom-left corner.
The centre of the top edge.
The centre of the bottom edge.
The centre of the right edge.
The centre of the left edge.

The centre. A legend inside a plot area at this location covers the data at the
centre of the plot.
The corner that overlaps the least data.

LegendSample.description:
The sample of a legend item that stands for no artist.

In JSON a sample is an object whose `type` names the variant, such as
`{"type": "swatch", "color": "#e69f00"}`.

oneOf.description:
A sample drawn as the sample of a series is drawn: a horizontal line with a
marker at its centre. A line whose dash is `none` draws only the marker, and a
marker whose shape is `none` draws only the line. A line colour of `auto` is the
ink in which the axes and labels of the figure are drawn, because the item belongs
to no axes whose colour order could supply one, and a marker colour of `auto`
takes the line colour, as it does for a series.

marker.description: The style of the marker at the centre of the line.

oneOf.description:
A square of a colour outlined in thin black, smaller than its row so that a
margin separates it from the swatches of neighbouring rows. It is the sample that
the category of a categorical scale draws, so in a legend panel a swatch of the
same label and colour as a category is merged with the entry of the category.

Levels.description: The field values at which contours are drawn.

oneOf.description: Levels are chosen at nice values spanning the data range.
Levels are given explicitly.

The range is computed from the data. Axis limits are rounded outwards to ticks, except where only the grid of a
contour or surface sets the x or y range, which then ends exactly at the grid.
The range is fixed.

max.description: The upper bound of the range.

min.description: The lower bound of the range.

LineStyle.description: The style of a stroked line.

dash.description: The dash pattern of the line.

oneOf.description: No marker is drawn.
A circle.
An axis-aligned square.
A square rotated by 45 degrees.
A triangle pointing upwards.
A triangle pointing downwards.
A plus sign.
A diagonal cross.
A small filled dot.
A vertical tick, a stroke as tall as the marker size (`'|'` in Matplotlib).
A horizontal tick, a stroke as wide as the marker size (`'_'` in Matplotlib).

MarkerStyle.description: The style of the markers drawn at data points.

edge.description: The colour of the marker outline.

face.description: The colour of the marker interior.

size_pt.description: The marker size in points, measured as the width of the marker.

NdArray.description: A dense, row-major, n-dimensional array of 64-bit floating-point values or of 8-bit unsigned integers.

element.description: The element type of the values: u8 for 8-bit unsigned integers, written as integers, or f64 for 64-bit floating-point values, which is also what an absent or null element means.

shape.description: The length of each dimension, outermost first.

values.description: The values in row-major order. A non-finite floating-point value is written as null and read back as NaN; an 8-bit value is an integer from 0 to 255 and is never null.

NdArrayElement.description:
The element type of an array: 64-bit floating-point values or 8-bit unsigned
integers.

In JSON the element is the string `"f64"` or `"u8"`, which is also how it is
displayed.

oneOf.description: 64-bit floating-point values.
8-bit unsigned integers.

Node.description:
A node that can be inserted into a figure, with its subtree.

In JSON a node is an object with one property, named after its kind in
`snake_case`, that holds the node, such as `{"panel": {"id": 6, ...}}`.

oneOf.description: A data array, which artists refer to by its identifier.
A colour scale, which colour-mapped artists refer to by its identifier.

An axes with its artists, boxed in a [`Node`] because an axes is much larger
than any other node.
A panel, which occupies cells of the tile layout and holds one key.
An artist, which an axes holds.

NodeId.description:
A stable identifier of a node: the figure, a data array, an axes, an artist or a
panel.

Every kind of node shares one identifier space, so node identifiers are unique within
a figure whatever the kind of node. They remain unchanged when the figure is saved and
loaded, so that interaction state, links, selections and the references between nodes
(such as an artist's reference to its data) refer to nodes across sessions.

Orientation.description:
The direction in which bars and stairs extend.

The category axis is the axis along which the positions of bars, and the edges or
samples of stairs, lie; the value axis is the axis along which their values lie.

oneOf.description:
Positions and edges lie along x and values along y, so that bars stand upright
(bar).
Positions and edges lie along y and values along x, so that bars lie flat (barh).

OutOfRange.description:
What is drawn for a value that a colour scale cannot place within its range: a value
below or above the range, outside the entries, or not finite.

Each category of such values holds a policy of its own (see [`ColorScaleOutOfRange`]),
so that, for example, non-finite values may be tolerated while values outside the
range are refused, or the reverse.

oneOf.description:
Such a value is a validation error, so the figure is refused until the data is
corrected.
Nothing is drawn for the value.

The value takes the nearest end colour of the scale: its first colour below the
range and its last colour above it. An index outside the entries of an indexed or
categorical scale is truncated toward zero and then clamped to the first or last
entry. A non-finite value has no nearest end, so at the `non_finite` category a
clamp draws nothing.
The value is drawn in a fixed colour.

color.description: The colour in which the value is drawn.

Panel.description:
A node of the figure that occupies cells of the tile layout, as an axes does, and
holds one key, such as a legend.

A panel is placed, fitted and checked against the layout in the same way whatever its
content; the content decides only what is drawn in it and how large that is.

align.description:
Where the content is placed within the panel. Along the span of a colourbar shorter
than the span, it also places the bar: a location that names an end of the span
pushes the bar to that end, and any other location centres it.

cell.description: The cells of the figure's tile layout that the panel occupies.

id.description: The node identifier of the panel, unique within the figure.

title.description:
A heading drawn at the top of the panel's content, or `None` for no heading. In a
boxed legend it lies inside the border, above the entries; above a standing colourbar
that spans plots, it lies in the margin above them, as an axes title does.

title_align.description:
How the title is aligned with the content it heads: with its left edge, its centre
or its right edge.

PanelColorbar.description:
A colourbar held by a panel: a colour scale shown as a bar that runs along the panel's
cell span, inset by the aligned margins of the rows or columns it spans, so that a bar
spanning a row or column of axes is measured against their drawn plot boxes.

The bar holds no colours, limits or ticks of its own: those belong to the scale, so that
every bar of one scale agrees with every other and with the artists drawn through it.

length.description:
The length of the bar, its keys included, as a fraction of the span of the drawn
plot boxes beside it, or `None` for the automatic length: the whole span for a
standing bar and half of it for a lying one. A fraction is a finite number greater
than 0 and at most 1. The bar is placed along the span by the panel's `align`.

orientation.description: Whether the bar stands along the panel's rows or lies along its columns.

scale.description: The colour scale that the bar shows.

title_placement.description: Where the title of the scale is drawn beside the bar.

PanelContent.description:
What a panel holds.

In JSON the content is an object whose `type` names the variant and whose `value`
holds it, such as `{"type": "legend", "value": {"boxed": true, ...}}`.

oneOf.description: A legend, which lists the entries of every axes whose legend names the panel.
A colourbar, which shows a colour scale along the cells of the panel.

PanelLegend.description:
The legend content of a panel, which lists the entries of every axes whose legend
names the panel.

Where the panel lies and where its content sits in it are properties of the
[`Panel`](crate::Panel); a legend content says only what is listed and how.

boxed.description:
Whether the area of the panel is outlined by a border drawn as the box of an
axes is drawn. The area of a panel is aligned with the plot areas of the axes in
its rows and columns, so the border continues the edges of their boxes. The
border has no background, and the entries are kept inset from it.

entries.description:
Which entries the panel lists, and in what order: the labelled artists of every
axes that names the panel, merged by label and look, in the reading order of the
layout, or an explicit list of items. An item that names an artist may name an
artist of any axes of the figure.

The property is omitted from JSON when the entries are automatic.

layout.description: How the entries are arranged in columns.

PanelLocation.description:
The placement of the content of a panel within the panel.

The locations are those of a legend inside a plot area, under the same names, except
that there is no `best`: a cell holds no data for the content to avoid.

oneOf.description: The centre.
The centre of the top edge.
The centre of the bottom edge.
The centre of the right edge.
The centre of the left edge.
The top-right corner.
The top-left corner.
The bottom-right corner.
The bottom-left corner.

Parameter.description:
A named value that describes a figure, such as the Reynolds number of the flow that
it shows or the name of the solver that produced its data.

Parameters do not affect drawing. They exist so that collections of figures can be
sorted, filtered and searched. In JSON, a parameter is an object whose `type` names
its kind and whose `value` holds the value, such as `{"type": "number", "value":
100000.0}`, so that the kind survives JSON's single number type.

oneOf.description: A boolean.
A signed 64-bit integer.
A double-precision floating-point number, which must be finite.
A string of Unicode text.

PerBar.description:
A number given once for every bar of a series or once per bar: where the bars of a
series start along the value axis.

On a logarithmic value axis a base that is not positive has no place, so such a bar is
drawn from the low edge of the plot area instead, with a warning.

oneOf.description: Every bar starts at the same value.

Each bar starts at its own value, one per bar, which draws floating bars and the
parts of a stack.

PixelRange.description:
The coordinates of the centres of the first and last pixels of an image along one
axis of its plane.

With `n` pixels along the axis the pitch is `(last − first) / (n − 1)`, so the image
covers `first − pitch / 2` to `last + pitch / 2`; a single pixel has a pitch of 1
whatever its range. A `last` less than `first` mirrors the image along the axis. Both
centres must be finite, and they may coincide only when the image has one pixel
along the axis, as validation checks.

first.description: The coordinate of the centre of the first pixel.

last.description: The coordinate of the centre of the last pixel.

PolarAngle.description: How the polar angle of a spherical axes is measured.

oneOf.description: The angle above the X–Y plane, as a latitude: 0 on the plane and a quarter turn at +Z.
The angle down from +Z, as a zenith angle: 0 at +Z and half a turn at −Z.

PolarView.description:
How the angles of a polar or cylindrical axes are measured, and where its sector and
hole lie on the page.

angle_units.description: The data units of the angle carried by x.

hole.description:
The fraction of the rim radius left empty at the centre, at least 0 and less than 1.
The lower radial limit lies on the edge of the hole.

radial_axis_angle.description:
The angle, in the data units of x, of the spoke along which the radial tick labels
are drawn, or `null` to draw them halfway between the first two angular ticks.

zero_deg.description:
The direction on the page in which angle 0 points, in degrees anticlockwise from
east in polar axes, or from the +X edge of the box in cylindrical axes; any finite
number.

oneOf.description: A two-dimensional Cartesian axes.
A three-dimensional Cartesian axes viewed through an orthographic camera.
A two-dimensional polar axes, in which x is the angle and y the radius.

polar.description: How angles are measured and where the sector and the hole lie on the page.

oneOf.description:
A three-dimensional cylindrical axes viewed through an orthographic camera, in which
x is the angle, y the radius and z the height along the central axis.

polar.description: How angles are measured and where angle 0 points.

oneOf.description:
A three-dimensional spherical axes viewed through an orthographic camera, in which x
is the azimuth, y the polar angle and z the radius.

spherical.description: How the two angles are measured.

PropertyPath.description: The address of a property within a node: Protocol Buffers field names separated by dots, such as x.limits.min.

Quiver.description:
Arrows representing a vector field at data points.

The position arrays and the component arrays hold one value per arrow and must
have the same number of elements.

head_size.description: The length of each arrow head as a fraction of its arrow's length.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

line.description: The style of the arrow shafts and heads.

scale.description: How vector lengths are scaled into arrow lengths.

u.description: The x components of the vectors.

v.description: The y components of the vectors.

w.description:
The z components of the vectors, allowed only in 3D axes; when absent in 3D
axes the vectors lie in horizontal planes.

x.description: The x coordinates of the arrow tails.

y.description: The y coordinates of the arrow tails.

z.description:
The z coordinates of the arrow tails, allowed only in 3D axes; when absent in
3D axes the tails lie in the plane z = 0.

QuiverScale.description: How quiver vector lengths are scaled into arrow lengths.

oneOf.description: Arrows are scaled so that the longest does not overlap its neighbours.
The automatic scale is multiplied by a factor.

value.description: The multiplier applied to the automatic scale.

oneOf.description: Arrows are drawn with the vectors' lengths in data units.

ScalarImage.description:
A scalar image: a raster of pixels, each holding one number that its colour scale maps
to a colour (image with an indexed array, and imagesc).

The scale decides what the numbers mean: through a continuous or discrete scale they
are values between limits, and through an indexed or categorical scale they are
indices of entries. A pixel whose number the scale cannot place (below or above its
range, outside its entries, or not finite) is drawn as the policy of that category of
the scale says. An image is drawn as flat, uninterpolated pixels rather than as a
mesh, so it is planar: it lies in one of the coordinate planes of its axes, where its
[`placement`](ScalarImage::placement) puts it.

alpha.description:
The alpha of every pixel, a two-dimensional array with the same shape as
`values`, or `None` for pixels that are uniformly opaque before
[`opacity`](ScalarImage::opacity) applies. The array may hold floating-point values
from 0 to 1 or 8-bit values from 0 to 255, as the components of a true-colour image
may. A value outside the range is clamped to it, and a pixel whose alpha is not
finite is transparent. The alpha also applies to a pixel drawn in the fixed colour
of an out-of-range policy.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

color_scale.description:
The colour scale through which the numbers are mapped. A scalar image always maps
its numbers, so a figure in which it names no scale is invalid.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

opacity.description:
The opacity of the image, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies
the alpha of every pixel: the alpha of its colour and, when present, its value
in [`alpha`](ScalarImage::alpha).

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

placement.description: Where the pixels lie in the axes.

values.description:
The numbers, a two-dimensional array of shape `[ny, nx]`, so that the number of
the pixel in row `j` and column `i` is at index `j * nx + i`. The array may hold
floating-point values or 8-bit values; an 8-bit value is mapped as the whole
number it denotes.

Scale.description: The mapping from data values to positions along an axis.

oneOf.description: Positions are proportional to values.

Positions are proportional to the base-10 logarithm of values; non-positive
values are not drawn.

Series.description:
A series of data points, drawn as a line through them, as markers at them, or as both
(plot, plot3, loglog, semilogx, semilogy, scatter, scatter3).

The x, y and (in 3D) z arrays hold one value per point and must have the same number
of elements. Non-finite positions break the line. The line is drawn unless its dash is
`none` or its colour is `none`, and the markers are drawn unless their shape is
`none`, so a plot is a series without markers and a scatter is a series without a
line.

base.description:
The value of y down to which the area under the line is filled, or `None` for no
base. The base is read in the coordinates of y, so with y in axes-fraction
coordinates a base of 0 is the bottom edge of the plot area.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

clip.description:
Whether the artist is clipped to the plot area. When false, clipping is released
only along a dimension in axes-fraction coordinates, so that markers can sit on or
beyond an edge of the axes; along a dimension in data coordinates the artist stays
clipped to the plot area, so an artist in data coordinates along both dimensions
is always clipped, and so is every artist of a 3D axes.

color_data.description:
The values that colour the series through its colour scale, or `None` for a
series of fixed colours. With one value per point, each marker takes the colour of
its point and each segment of a colormapped line is a gradient between the colours
of its two points. With one value per segment (one fewer than the points), each
segment of the line takes the colour of its value and the markers take their own
colours; this form is valid only when the series draws a line.

color_scale.description:
The colour scale through which the colour data is mapped. A series with colour
data must name one; a series without colour data maps nothing.

fill.description:
The colour of the area between the line through the points and the base, or none
(the default) for no fill. A fill other than none needs a base, and is invalid in
three-dimensional axes. An automatic fill takes the colour of the series; a
colormapped fill is invalid, because the colour data colours points and segments
and not the area beneath them.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is none, and is none when JSON omits it.

fill_opacity.description:
The opacity of the fill, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies the
alpha of its colour.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

line.description:
The style of the line through the points. Its colour is the colour of the series,
which an automatic marker face or edge follows; a colormapped colour takes the
colours of the colour data.

marker.description: The style of the markers at the points.

size_data.description:
The diameter of each marker in points, one value per point, or `None` for markers
that all take `marker.size_pt`. The marker size remains the size of the legend
key.

x.description: The x coordinates of the points.

x_coords.description:
How the x values are placed: as data along the x axis, or as fractions of the
plot area's width. Anything other than `data` is allowed only in 2D axes.

y.description: The y coordinates of the points.

y_coords.description:
How the y values are placed: as data along the y axis, or as fractions of the
plot area's height. Anything other than `data` is allowed only in 2D axes.

z.description:
The z coordinates of the points, allowed only in 3D axes; when absent in 3D
axes the points lie in the plane z = 0.

SphericalView.description: How the two angles of a spherical axes are measured.

angle_units.description: The data units of the azimuth carried by x and of the polar angle carried by y.

polar_angle.description: Whether the polar angle is measured up from the X–Y plane or down from +Z.

Stairs.description:
A stepped outline through values held between edges or at samples (stairs, step).

Stairs draw the outline that a histogram of steps draws: along the category axis the
outline runs through each value across its step, and it joins neighbouring steps with
segments along the value axis. A value that is not finite breaks the outline. With a
base, the outline drops to the base at both ends and may be filled down to it.

base.description:
The value along the value axis to which the outline drops at both ends, or `None`
for an open outline that starts and ends at the first and last values.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

binning.description:
How the histogram that the stairs draw was binned from its samples, or `None` for
stairs that were not made from samples (ADR 0029). The record is descriptive: it is
read by datatips to report the count and density of each step and is never edited.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

data.description: The steps: values between edges, or values at samples.

fill.description:
The colour of the area between the outline and the base, or none for no fill. A
fill other than none needs a base; a colormapped fill is invalid.

fill_opacity.description:
The opacity of the fill, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies the
alpha of its colour.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

line.description:
The style of the outline, whose automatic colour is the next colour of the colour
order. A colormapped colour is invalid, because stairs have no colour data and no
colour scale.

line_opacity.description:
The opacity of the outline, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies
the alpha of its colour.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

orientation.description: Whether the steps lie along x, with values along y, or the reverse.

StairsData.description: The steps of stairs: values between edges, or values at samples.

oneOf.description:
Each value holds between two neighbouring edges, as the counts of a histogram hold
between its bin edges (Matplotlib's `stairs`).

edges.description:
The edges of the steps along the category axis, one more than the values:
finite and strictly monotonic, increasing or decreasing.

oneOf.description:
Each value holds at a sample, and the step from one value to the next occurs where
`step` places it (MATLAB's `stairs` and Matplotlib's `step`).

step.description: Where each step occurs relative to its samples.

x.description:
The positions of the samples along the category axis, one per value: finite
and strictly monotonic, increasing or decreasing.

StepAt.description:
Where the step of stairs through samples occurs relative to its samples, as the
`where` argument of Matplotlib's `step` places it.

oneOf.description:
Each value holds from the previous sample up to its own, so the step occurs at the
earlier sample.

Each value holds from its own sample up to the next, so the step occurs at the
later sample.

Each value holds from halfway to the previous sample to halfway to the next, so the
step occurs midway between the samples.

Surface.description:
A surface of quadrilateral faces over a grid (surf, mesh, surface).

A surface is valid in either projection. In a three-dimensional axes `z` is the height
of every node. In a two-dimensional axes the surface is seen from directly above, so
that `z` positions nothing and the surface is a pseudocolour plot of its colour data.
A field of `ny` by `nx` nodes draws `(ny - 1)` by `(nx - 1)` faces, so a field with a
single row or a single column draws nothing.

c.description:
The colour data of every node, with the same shape as `z`; when absent the
surface is coloured by `z`.

color_scale.description:
The colour scale through which the colour data is mapped. A surface whose faces or
edges are colormapped or automatic must name one.

edge.description: The colour of the face edges.

edge_alpha.description:
The alpha of the face edges at every node, an array of 64-bit floating-point
values with the same shape as `z`, or `None` for edges that are uniformly opaque
before [`edge_opacity`](Surface::edge_opacity) applies. The edges of a face take
the mean of the edge alpha at its four corners, clamped and made transparent by
a non-finite value as the face alpha is. It may name the same array as
`face_alpha`.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

edge_opacity.description:
The opacity of the face edges, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which
multiplies the alpha of every edge: the edge colour's own alpha and, when
present, the [`edge_alpha`](Surface::edge_alpha) of the face it borders.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

edge_width_pt.description: The width of the face edges in points.

face_alpha.description:
The alpha of the faces at every node, an array of 64-bit floating-point values
with the same shape as `z`, or `None` for faces that are uniformly opaque before
[`face_opacity`](Surface::face_opacity) applies. A face takes the mean of the
alpha at its four corners, as it takes the mean of their colour data. A value
outside `[0, 1]` is clamped to that range, and a face with a corner whose alpha
is not finite is transparent.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is absent.

face_opacity.description:
The opacity of the faces, from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), which multiplies
the alpha of every face: the face colour's own alpha and, when present, the
[`face_alpha`](Surface::face_alpha) of the face.

The property is omitted from JSON when it is 1, and is 1 when JSON omits it.

grid.description: The grid on which the surface is sampled.

id.description: The node identifier of the artist, unique within the figure.

label.description: The label drawn beside the artist in a legend.

z.description:
The field, a two-dimensional array of shape `[ny, nx]`: the height of every node in
a three-dimensional axes, and the colour data of every node unless `c` is given.

Text.description: A piece of text, stored as its source so that renderers typeset it lazily.

content.description:
The source text. With the LaTeX interpreter, segments delimited by `$…$`
are typeset as mathematics and the remainder as plain text.

interpreter.description: How the source text is interpreted.

TickLabels.description: What is written at the major ticks of an axis.

oneOf.description: Each tick is labelled with its value, formatted for the scale of the axis.
The ticks are drawn without labels, and no space is reserved for labels.

Each tick is labelled with the text at the same position in the list. Valid only
with [`Ticks::Values`] holding as many values as there are texts.

Ticks.description:
Where the major ticks of an axis are placed.

Ticks never change the limits of an axis: automatic limits are computed as they are
for automatic ticks, and a tick that lies outside the limits is not drawn.

oneOf.description: The ticks are chosen at round values from the limits and the length of the axis.

A tick at every value `origin + k × step`, for every integer `k`, that lies
within the limits.

origin.description: A value at which a tick is placed if it lies within the limits; finite.

step.description: The distance between neighbouring ticks, in data units; finite and positive.

oneOf.description:
A tick at each of the given values that lies within the limits; every value is
finite, and positive on a logarithmic axis.

TileLayout.description:
The grid of cells in which the axes and panels of a figure are placed.

A row or column is either weighted or fitted to the panels it holds. The margins
that the axes reserve for their tick labels, axis labels and titles are taken out of
the figure first. A fitted row then takes the height that the panels in it need
for their entries, and a fitted column the width. The plot areas of the weighted rows
share the rest of the height, and those of the weighted columns the rest of the width,
in proportion to their weights, so that plot areas of equal weight are of equal size. A
row or column without a size, because the list of sizes is shorter than the number of
rows or columns, has a weight of one, so that empty lists give plot areas of equal size.

col_weights.description:
The sizes of the columns, from the left: a finite positive weight, or fitted to the
panels in the column. A column without a size has a weight of one, and there
are no more sizes than columns.

The property is omitted from JSON when there are no sizes.

cols.description: The number of columns; at least one.

row_weights.description:
The sizes of the rows, from the top: a finite positive weight, or fitted to the
panels in the row. A row without a size has a weight of one, and there are
no more sizes than rows.

The property is omitted from JSON when there are no sizes.

rows.description: The number of rows; at least one.

TitleAlign.description:
How a title is aligned with what it heads: the title of an axes with its plot area, and
the title of a panel with the panel's content.

oneOf.description: The title is centred over the plot area or the content.
The left edge of the title is on the left edge of the plot area or the content.
The right edge of the title is on the right edge of the plot area or the content.

TrackSize.description:
The size of one row or column of a tile layout.

In JSON a size is an object whose `type` names the variant, such as
`{"type": "weight", "value": 2.0}` or `{"type": "fit"}`.

oneOf.description:
A share of the height or width that the fitted rows or columns leave, in
proportion to this weight, which must be finite and positive.

The size of the content of the panels that lie in this row or column
alone, with their borders and the margins that align them with the plot areas
around them. An axes cannot lie in fitted rows or columns alone, because an axes
has no content size of its own.

Value.description:
The value of a property, as set by [`Edit::Set`](crate::Edit::Set) and returned by
[`Figure::get`](crate::Figure::get).

There is one variant for each type of value that a property path can address, and
the variant [`Value::Unset`], which clears an optional property. The type of a value
is checked against its path when an edit is applied, so a value of the wrong type is
rejected then rather than when the value is constructed.

Reading a property converts the IR value into a variant of this type, so a property
of a type that has no variant cannot be read, and a new value type in the IR must
gain a variant here before its properties can be edited.

In JSON a value is an object whose `type` names the variant in `snake_case` and whose
`value` holds the value in its usual JSON form, such as
`{"type": "limits", "value": {"type": "manual", "min": 0, "max": 1}}`; an unset value
is `{"type": "unset"}`.

How a 2D axes keeps a fixed aspect.

A marker shape.
How the values of one dimension of a series are placed.
A list of sizes of the rows or columns of the tile layout.
The grid of a contour or surface.
The levels of a contour.
The placement of a contour in three-dimensional axes.
The scaling of quiver arrows.

The centres of the first and last pixels of an image along an axis.

View3d.description: The orthographic camera view of a three-dimensional axes.

azimuth_deg.description:
The rotation about the vertical axis in degrees, measured counterclockwise
from the negative y axis when viewed from above.

elevation_deg.description: The angle of the view direction above the x-y plane in degrees, from -90 to 90.

pan_x.description:
The horizontal offset of the projected box as a fraction of the plot area's
width, increasing to the right.

pan_y.description:
The vertical offset of the projected box as a fraction of the plot area's
height, increasing downwards.

zoom.description: The magnification of the projected box, where 1 fits the box to the plot area.

description:
An ordered list of edits that are applied together or not at all.

A transaction is encoded as the Protocol Buffers message `Transaction` of
`ironlab/ir/v0/edit.proto`, and as JSON with the same structure.

edits.description: The edits, in the order in which they are applied.
